message.content:
I don’t have direct access to your network, so I can’t tell you what your current download/upload speeds are.  
The easiest way to find out is to run a quick speed‑test yourself. Here’s how you can do it:

---

### 1. Use a Web Site (easiest)

1. Open a browser and go to one of the popular speed‑test sites:
   * https://www.speedtest.net/
   * https://fast.com/ (by Netflix)
2. Click “Go” or “Start Test”.
3. Wait for the test to finish – it will show you the download speed, upload speed, and ping.

---

### 2. Run a Command‑Line Test (if you prefer terminal)

If you’re comfortable with the command line, you can install the official Speedtest CLI and run it from your terminal.

#### On Windows

```powershell
# Install the Speedtest CLI (requires PowerShell 5+)
winget install -e --id Ookla.Speedtest

# Run a test
speedtest
```

#### On macOS / Linux

```bash
# Install the Speedtest CLI (requires Homebrew on macOS or apt on Ubuntu)
brew install speedtest-cli          # macOS
sudo apt-get install speedtest-cli  # Ubuntu/Debian

# Run a test
speedtest
```

The output will look something like this:

```
Testing from Your ISP (Your City)...
Retrieving speedtest.net configuration...
Testing download speed........................................
Download:  85.23 Mbit/s
Testing upload speed..........................................
Upload:    12.45 Mbit/s
Ping:      15.3 ms
```

---

### 3. Using a Browser Extension

There are also browser extensions that display your speed in real time (e.g., “Speedtest by Ookla” for Chrome/Edge). Just add the extension and click the icon whenever you want to see your current speed.

---

**What to Do With the Results**

* If the speeds are lower than what your ISP advertises, you may want to contact your provider or troubleshoot (restart router, check cables, etc.).
* If you’re doing bandwidth‑heavy tasks (streaming, gaming, large downloads), compare the numbers to the minimum requirements for those services.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the results or troubleshooting any issues!
